title: Static-equivalence quotient and separating finite dynamic estimand
question: When two finite candidate dynamics share the same registered static signature, can a reusable equivalence relation and a candidate-neutral finite dynamic estimand expose non-identifiability without changing the existing forward or inverse methods?
purpose: Turn the existing R-193/R-200 witness into a quotient-interface result for T-061 dynamic-owner intake. The quotient records what static data cannot identify; it does not select a physical candidate or supply the missing source-owned dynamics.

finite_contract.state: abstract finite two-coordinate Gaussian proxy inherited from the registered static witness
finite_contract.regulator: finite two-coordinate witness only; no cutoff limit
finite_contract.boundary_condition: not applicable in the abstract witness

quotient_contract.quotient_object: Setoid of Dynamics modulo static-equivalence classes
quotient_contract.separating_estimator: D_probe at the fixed finite probe (1,0)

assumptions: The finite static signature is exactly the registered two-coordinate hessian/covariance pair.
The two diagonal factor pairs are comparison dynamics only and are not identified with a canonical production generator.
Static equivalence forgets dynamic factors by definition and therefore describes an equivalence class, not a unique model.
The probe is a finite algebraic one-step proxy; the time label is explicitly not physical time.
Exact rational arithmetic and the pinned Lean toolchain are available for the declared finite witness.
missing_assumptions: A hash-pinned source-owned generator or transfer operator.
A state, physical projection, time boundary, heat-root map and filtration owned by the production source.
A raw-current spatial intertwiner and one-use production q-ledger.
A complete F_reg/F_lim/F_eff/F_obs observation map with uncertainty and nuisance model.
Regulator and volume stability, prospective holdout data, and an immutable acceptance rule.
Any identification with QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity, a physical vacuum, continuum dynamics or a mass gap.
evidence_level: T0 / EXACT FINITE STATIC-EQUIVALENCE QUOTIENT WITH INDEPENDENT, HOSTILE AND LEAN CROSS-CHECKS
non_claims: No unique microscopic dynamics is selected by the static signature.
No source-owned production dynamics, heat semigroup, filtration, raw-current map or q-ledger is supplied.
No observation likelihood, covariance, holdout prediction or empirical validation is performed.
No physical candidate, Pre-A, Sector-A, C6, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity, continuum, cosmic-origin or mass-gap conclusion follows.
hostile_mutations: replace static equivalence by equality of the full dynamics
change the probe to a non-separating zero probe
make the two comparison factor pairs equal
change the static covariance so the inverse relation fails
promote the static equivalence class to a unique selection
promote the T0 interface to claim-bearing evidence
admit a source-owned production generator without its owner contract

lean_crosscheck.role: Lean checks the equivalence-relation laws, inverse static signature, distinct finite representatives and separating one-step proxy; it does not provide a physical dynamics or observation map.

boundary: R-448 is a finite abstract quotient interface. It proves that the registered static signature admits a non-singleton comparison class and that a declared finite one-step proxy separates two representatives. It does not choose a representative, infer Pre-A from observations, supply any missing production owner, or close T-061, T-054, C6, Sector-A, QFT, Yang--Mills, gravity, continuum or mass-gap gates.
next_action: Use the quotient contract as the fixed T-061 intake boundary. Admit a candidate only after its source-owned generator, state/projection, boundary, heat-root/filtration, raw-current intertwiner, q-ledger and observation map are hash-pinned; otherwise keep the surviving static-equivalence class and do not add another finite mobility table.
